reasons: Wrong metric: postgresql.rollbacks counts rolled-back transactions, while the Datadog query measures rows hot-updated (heap-only tuple updates). Filtering rollbacks by operation="hot_upd" does not produce that quantity.

The candidate never checks whether an OTel metric for row operations (e.g. postgresql.operations with operation="hot_upd") exists. If one does, the converter should translate to it; if not, the request should be blocked with MISSING_METRIC_MAPPING.

Template variables are dropped: $db (prefix db, observed label postgresql_database_name) and $host (prefix host, observed label host_name) should become matchers, so the candidate covers a different set of series than the request.
Grouping by postgresql_database_name matches the Datadog 'by {db}' and uses an observed label, but the aggregation and series are only correct if the underlying metric is correct, which it is not.
